meta.name: andalus
meta.description: One person's Windows terminal environment, expressed as data instead of as a script.
notes: JSON rather than YAML for this document because ConvertFrom-Json is built into every supported engine, and a fresh machine has no YAML parser. The winget file next to this one is YAML only because winget requires it, and this project never parses it.

Font sha256 values are intentionally blank, and that blankness is load-bearing. Fetching an archive over TLS proves who served it, not what it contains. Rather than trust the transport, apply does not install fonts at all: it reports them with the command that would. Filling these in is the stated condition for adopting font installation, recorded in ADR-0006.

Every resource kind in this document is now evaluated by doctor and plan. apply converges four of them - terminal.fragment, terminal.asset, omp.theme and shell.profile - and reports the other four with the exact command that would satisfy them. The principle the earlier version of this note was protecting has not changed and still governs: a resource that was not checked must be reported as unverified rather than omitted, because a partial plan that reads like a converged machine is a lie the user has no way to detect.

terminal.global is refused on principle rather than deferred for want of an adapter. Those values live in the user's own settings.json, and owning that file is the original sin this project exists to avoid: Windows Terminal rewrites it on its own schedule, it is JSON-with-comments that a naive parse-and-reserialize destroys, and its path depends on which channel is installed. doctor and plan report drift in defaultProfile and theme. Nothing writes them.

The Andalus palette is authored, not derived. Its sixteen colours come from manuscript illumination pigments: lapis lazuli for blue, gold leaf for yellow, vermilion for red, Persian turquoise for cyan, aubergine for purple, on a parchment foreground. The Volcanic Heat scheme it replaces had fourteen of its sixteen colours guessed. None of these are.

The prompt contains no Arabic words, and that is deliberate. Windows Terminal renders Arabic left to right even where it shapes and joins the letters correctly, so any Arabic string in a prompt displays reversed, and displays differently across builds. The theme uses three standalone ornaments from Arabic Presentation Forms instead: U+FD3E and U+FD3F ornate parentheses, and U+06DE start of Rub el Hizb. All three are bidi class Other Neutral with no joining behaviour, so they render the same in every direction context. Arabic calligraphy reaches the window as a background image, where it is pixels and bidi never applies.

The prompt now depends on Nerd Font glyphs. This reverses an earlier decision recorded here, and the reversal is not free. The rounded segment caps U+E0B6 and U+E0B4, and the os, folder, branch and clock icons, all live in the Private Use Area and exist only in a patched font. On a machine where the font resource has not been applied yet the prompt renders as replacement boxes, which is a real bootstrap ordering problem the previous zero-glyph design did not have. doctor verifying that the font family is genuinely installed is therefore load-bearing now rather than informational.

Font detection cannot be done by comparing the family name to the registry, and one full release was shipped believing otherwise. Nerd Fonts registers abbreviated families - CaskaydiaCove NF, NFM, NFP - plus filename-shaped values such as CaskaydiaCoveNerdFontMono-Regular. The verbose name declared here, CaskaydiaCove Nerd Font Mono, appears in the registry not at all: it is name ID 16, the typographic family, while the registry and GDI store name ID 1. Measured on the author's machine: 48 registry values, four naming conventions, three WPF families, one typeface. Keep the verbose name here anyway, because it is what Windows Terminal displays and what a user would type.

The frosted panels behind the text in the reference image are not a Windows Terminal capability. Terminal paints one uniform character grid: there is no per-region background, no rounded rectangle and no drop shadow anywhere in the settings schema. Those panels have to be painted into the background image. This fixes the requirement for the asset: a dark translucent wash across the left two thirds so text stays legible, with the artwork weighted to the right.

backgroundImage composites on top of the acrylic layer rather than beneath it, so image opacity and window frosting trade against each other directly. At backgroundImageOpacity 1.0 the blur is completely hidden and the window is frosted only in the settings file. 0.85 is the compromise being tested.

useAcrylic with opacity 72 is a request, not a guarantee. Windows ignores it when Transparency effects are turned off in Settings, and suppresses it under Battery Saver. doctor must report the effective state rather than the requested one, because a converged terminal.fragment is not the same thing as a window that actually looks frosted. Not yet built.

Deploying this fragment is not the same as seeing it. Windows Terminal layers defaults, then fragments, then the user's settings.json, and the last layer to mention a property wins. On the author's machine settings.json sets colorScheme, font face, font size, line height and cell width directly on the target profile, so every one of those is overridden and the fragment is invisible until they are cleared with the reset arrow in Settings. doctor and apply both detect this and report it rather than showing a green check next to a change nobody can see.

Left padding cannot be used to keep terminal output clear of the calligraphy rail in the backdrop, and the next person to try should read this before raising the number. padding is absolute DIPs; the background image is scaled to the window. The rail therefore always sits at about 6.7 percent of the current width, so a value chosen for one window size drifts at every other. Measured cost of clearing it at 1920: 0.13 of contrast ratio gained at the worst pixel, 0.05 lost at the fifth percentile. It is a composition choice, not a legibility one.

The bootstrap one-liner works. Verified in production on 2026-08-11 in all three forms: the bare irm-pipe-iex, the TS_VERSION environment variable, and the scriptblock form with real parameters. An earlier version of this note listed three reasons it could not work and every one of them has been removed - the repository is public, v0.1.0 is published with an attached archive, and get.ps1 no longer declares mandatory parameters, which a pipe into Invoke-Expression can never supply. The remaining constraints are recorded in ADR-0005: no exit on any path, because under Invoke-Expression that closes the user's window, and no #Requires, because it is a directive for script files.
